source: RFC 0007 §5.4 (DR1-F-7, RC review round 1 area F: a lost write is diagnosable from the revision chain)
statement: A revision a document's index lists above its head was published and its head write then lost while the index entry written after it was kept, as a failover of a Redis Cluster primary loses one (a document's head and index live in different slots); nothing else leaves an index ahead of its head. On one primary, replication keeps the order of writes, so a failover that loses a head loses its index entry too, and only the data plane's regression signal tells of it. The reclamation pass looks for such revisions in every document before it reads the document's history; and a rebuild of an index from its head (a read of the history once a publish reused the number) hands over the entries not on the head's chain before it drops them, the last place they are listed. Each is logged at ERROR, counted (cosec.control.revisions.lost) and told to the change listeners once by the instance that finds it (HEAD_LOST, naming the change and its publisher from the lost revision's own provenance, the head as base and the lost revision as candidate). The control plane never moves a head forward again on its own: whoever published the change publishes it again or rolls back.
